newsitem.title: USA: District attorney charges six in California bombings.
newsitem.headline: District attorney charges six in California bombings.

text.p: Prosecutors formally charged six men Tuesday with involvement in two bombings that damaged a courthouse and a bank in a California town.

The men were charged with a variety of offenses, including possession, transportation and detonation of explosive devices, burglary, and conspiracy, Solano County District Attorney David Paulson said.
They were arraigned in municipal court and ordered held without bail pending a Feb 14 hearing, officials said.
The charges stem from two bombings in the last 10 days in Vallejo, 35 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco, that damaged a courthouse and a bank but caused no injuries.
Police disarmed a third bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite found outside a public library that also housed a police evidence room.

On Sunday, police seized 500 lbs (230 kg) of dynamite stored in a Vallejo garage and found a car with 61 sticks of dynamite in the trunk that investigators believe the bombers had wired up ready for use in another attack.

The men charged in the district attorney's 20-count complaint were Kevin Robinson, Army Osotonu, Oston Osotonu, Francis Ernestberg, Orlando Johnson, and Jason Pascual. They were arrested on Sunday and Monday.
Vallejo police said they believe Robinson hired two of the men to carry out the bombings to disrupt his trial on drugs charges that had been due to start in a nearby town Monday.

Robinson, Oston Osotonu, Ernestberg and Johnson will be prosecuted under California's tough "three strikes and you're out" law. If convicted on the charges, Paulson said the men would face imprisonment for life.
The district attorney's office said its investigation was ongoing and could lead to additional charges.
